slides.headline: Building Moon rockets was only the start.
Six decades of rocket power
slides.body: NASA has built rockets for over sixty years. Its Saturn rockets carried Apollo astronauts all the way to the Moon.

slides.headline: New rockets for the Moon
slides.body: NASA now builds the SLS rocket for Artemis. It also manages Moon landers to aid future trips to Mars.

slides.headline: Focus turns to nuclear drives
slides.body: NASA is advancing nuclear propulsion. This focus is expected to grow as NASA works to send humans to Mars.

slides.headline: NASA is looking far past the Moon.
slides.body: Nuclear power is expected to grow as NASA works toward Mars.

caption:
Building Moon rockets was only the start.

For more than sixty years, NASA has built rocket power. Its Saturn rockets carried astronauts to the Moon during Apollo.

The catch? The agency is now building new systems to carry us deeper into space. That includes the Artemis SLS rocket and Moon landers that support future trips to Mars.

The payoff? NASA is advancing nuclear power and propulsion. That focus is expected to grow as NASA works toward sending the first humans to Mars. 🚀

Source: NASA — NASA Names Stephen Cash Marshall Space Flight Center Director
